learning: If line_loss_events falls below about 1 per run and progress rises, keep base_speed 1.15 and test one further controller change, such as kd. If progress falls or line loss rises, return base_speed to 1.3, which is the proven value, and test line-loss handling instead.
notes: Reference geometry (iteration 1, reproduced in iterations 4 and 6) with base_speed lowered from 1.3 to 1.15 as the only change. Weights are matched to the sensor x order and sign convention.
rationale: The Builder holds the iteration 1 geometry: five 12 mm sensors at x = -0.03, -0.015, 0, 0.015, 0.03 m, y = 0.05 m, on a 0.12 m track with 0.03 m wheels, 0.6 kg mass and a 0.16 x 0.14 m body. This geometry has now raced three times with the same controller (iterations 1, 4 and 6) and scored 69.3241 each time, so it is reproducible. Re-racing the identical package would add no new information, so this iteration tests one controller change. Evidence for the controller lever: line loss has stayed at about 1 per run across every geometry (1.0 to 1.65), so sensor layout alone has not removed it. Iteration 1 lowered base_speed from 1.5 to 1.3 and kp from 3.0 to 2.5 and gained about 15 points, though that change was paired with the span change. Off-track failure at about 15 percent progress is the main score loss, so I lower base_speed further to 1.15 while keeping kp 2.5, kd 0.3, ki 0, last_direction line loss and the weights matched to the sensor x order. Sign check: positive x (left) carries a positive weight, so a line on the left steers left, as the contract requires. Single-variable change against the 69.32 reference, so any score change is attributable to base_speed. Expected result: line_loss_events falls toward or below 1 per run and progress rises a little, with a small loss of completion-time credit. This is a prediction, not a measurement. Risk: a slower base_speed may fail to finish within 3 s, which is accepted because the runs currently end off track well before the finish.
